edit.description: The grain flip, read and write. `hook_member_fields` (:628) stops minting one member per handler: each group yields ONE member carrying its lifted fields alone plus the group's ordered handler entries, so `RegistrationMember` (:73) gains a members column beside `fields` and `Manifest::parse` (:392-:397) fills it. The entries are carried kind-LESS — `Manifest::parse` sees only `&[&CollectionAddress]`, never a kind — so `EntryShape` (`src/kind.rs`:165) is NOT widened and its seven other construction sites do not move; the caller that knows the kind keys them. `hook_matcher_group` (:672) re-nests a group carrying N handlers instead of exactly one and stays the exact inverse; the round-trip unit test (:1040) re-baselines on a two-handler group.

`manifest_units` (:716) knows the kind, so it is where a group's kind-less handler entries become members: keyed `<hook-host-address>/handler/<position>` via `member_address::nested_address`, under the child kind the HOST kind's `templates` column names (the fact `claude_code_hook()` gains in the predecessor entry) rather than a name hard-coded in the read. `embedded_features_by_kind` (:1255) gains them as its second contributor beside the lock's `nested_member` rows, with raw JSON fields carried as read — NOT through `embedded_member_features` (:1299), which stringifies prose leaves, so a handler's `timeout`/`args`/`headers` keep their JSON types. A handler's values never reach the lock: a registration row drops its `fields` (`src/drift.rs`:5519, decision 0018) and the manifest is the read-back source, exactly as a hook's own fields already are.

The GroupArray write arm (:1274-:1292): one registration row is now one whole group, so its `fields` (:4354, seam-inbound) carry the group's lifted fields plus its handler array, and the arm appends one group per row rather than accumulating single-handler groups under a shared key. The comment at :1278-:1281 states the new accumulation rule.

The coverage census (:720-:722) counts nested members off `committed.nested_members` alone; a manifest-composed handler has no lock row, so it must be counted off the composed corpus or `handler` reads as `(0 embedded)` over a harness that has handlers. The embedded dispatcher at :435-:446 already runs the two greens over whatever `embedded_features_by_kind` returns.

`RegistrationMember`'s two consumers outside its own module: the lift's `entries` (:535) and `lifted_registration` (:2122), which builds a `LiftedMember` from one registration entry's flat fields. A lifted hook member now carries its group's handlers rather than one handler's fields inline. This is the compile-time half only — what the gate lift MINTS is HOOK-AUTHORS-ITS-HANDLERS' to move.

`hookDefaultContract` (:1809) drops the spread and becomes the event clause alone — the six now bind through `handler` only, retiring the transitional double binding HANDLER-IS-A-BUILT-IN-KIND-UNDER-HOOK named. `Hook` (:392) narrows to the group's own fields: `matcher` stays, the handler-table fields leave for `Handler`. `hook()`'s authoring signature and `tapHookRegistration` (:482) are HOOK-AUTHORS-ITS-HANDLERS' to move — this entry keeps them compiling against the narrowed interface.
Regenerated: `hook`'s clause rows shrink to the `event` enum, `handler`'s six stay. The header's contract arithmetic at :55-:60 moves with it.
The byte-compare covers the shrink; no new binding, the program already binds both kinds after the predecessor entry.

The suite's whole premise moves from per-handler members to per-group members: a two-handler group is one `hook` member with two `handler` children at `…/handler/0` and `…/handler/1`, a handler missing its `type` draws the finding under `handler` rather than `hook`, and a group's `matcher` stays the hook's own field. The suite is a module of the one `it` crate, so scaffolding is reached as `common::…` through `crate`.
Its `settings.json` fixtures carry `hooks` segments; any arm asserting a member count or a hook member's flat handler fields re-baselines to the group grain.

The corpus authors two hooks (`hook (2)` in its diagnostics snapshot); the expected change is the coverage line plus any finding whose kind label moves from `hook` to `handler`. Touch only if the renderer must move.
The `coverage.checked` line's kind census: `hook`'s count becomes its group count and `handler (N embedded)` joins, the spelling `citation (1 embedded)` already uses.
Declared for the fence: the corpus's emitted lock renders here and its `hook` registration rows are one-per-group after the flip. Re-baseline if the run moves a byte.
The `hook`/`handler` contract cases re-state the final split: `hookDefaultContract` is the event clause alone, `handlerDefaultContract` the six.

Its `hook({...})` programs spell the handler fields inline on the member (:1859, :1899, :2193-:2194) and break the moment `Hook` narrows; :2193-:2194 is the two-distinct-matcher pair the address entry then re-addresses.
Same: the `hook({ name: "PreToolUse", type, command })` program at :310 moves to the handler-carrying shape.

summary: A hook member is its whole matcher group, and each entry of the group's `hooks` array is a nested `handler` member keyed by position.

tests.asserts: a two-handler group reads as one `hook` member carrying its matcher plus `handler` members at `…/handler/0` and `…/handler/1`, a handler-level finding names the handler's address, and the group re-nests to byte-identical `settings.json`
the group-array read and its inverse round-trip a multi-handler group without collapsing or duplicating a group

acceptance: cargo test green (the gauntlet snapshots accepted), `pnpm --dir sdk test` green, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo fmt --all --check clean, and the self-host check (tests/it/cli.rs:296) still clean over this repo's committed surface.
notes: Decision 0075's grain, engine side. It lands alone safely: identity is still the bare event, so a group carrying two handlers stops minting two members at one address rather than starting to. The address discriminator is HOOK-NAME-JOINS-ITS-MATCHER, deliberately after — 0075's 'address and grain ship together' is the ban on the other order. scoped at 079c105e
